name: Voice deepfake kidnapping/wire-transfer scam (caller-ID spoofing)
source: Synthetic voice-scam case for the audio forensics pipeline (Track 03). The harness synthesizes the WAV from `audio_spec` at run time, so the repository never ships binary audio.

audio_spec.comment: Deterministic tone composition standing in for a deepfake voicemail: a 220 Hz sine 'voice' bed (steady machine pitch -> robotic_artifact), a clipped 330 Hz overlay (heavy_distortion), and a flat envelope with one unnaturally clean micro-gap (low energy variation + tiny silence ratio -> unnatural_cadence). Pure-python wave module; no external assets or seeds.

payload.text: Caller ID showed +65 8116 4472 (spoofed police number). Voicemail transcript: 'We have your son. Wire the transfer now or he stays with us. Do not call the police. Account number and card details for the drop. You have one hour.'

expected.notes_field: local spectral pass flags synthesis artifacts; the transcript/context regex sweep flags the kidnapping, wire-transfer, isolation, and credential script elements; offline mode records an explicit Gemini-unavailable note.

notes: Phone number is fake but format-valid so the redactor must catch it. Disclosed limitation: the pattern-based redactor cannot redact common words like 'son' (a family relationship is not a PII pattern); the hard assertions are the phone-number redaction and the audio findings.
